  • Bhava-pratyaya: For _videhas_ and _prakṛti-layas_
  • Ahiṁsā-pratiṣṭhāyāṁ tat-sannidhau vaira-tyāgaḥ 2.35*
  • When non-violence is ﬁrmly established, hostility is abandoned in the yogi’s presence.
  • _Achievement_: Ahiṁsā is not mere abstention from killing. When it becomes a state of
  • mind free from the very saṁskāra of harm, the yogi’s vibration of peace is so potent that
  • even natural enemies drop their enmity. Classical commentaries cite examples of tigers
  • and deer drinking together near sages. Psychologically, the yogi becomes incapable of
  • reaction, and the ﬁeld around him reﬂects that absence of violence. This is the ﬁrst sign
  • that yoga is not escapism, but changes the fabric of relationships.
  • Sit in _Daṇḍāsana_ with legs extended straight, spine erect, palms beside hips.
  • Start: Lie on your back in _Śavāsana_. Bend both knees, bring heels close to the
  • buttocks, hip-width apart. Feet ﬂat and parallel.
  • Start: Stand in _Tāḍāsana_ with feet hip-width, a wall 2-3 feet behind you.
questions.final_answer: Start: Stand in _Tāḍāsana_ with feet hip-width, a wall 2-3 feet behind you.

questions.question: Who is Iswara?
questions.solution_html:
• Upāya-pratyaya
  • Asamprajñāta samādhi is the pinnacle of _citta-vṛtti-nirodha_. By relinquishing even the
  • subtlest supports of meditation through para-vairāgya, the yogi enters seedless absorption
  • where only cessation remains. From this silence, the saṁskāras that bind consciousness
  • to rebirth are dissolved, and the _puruṣa_ stands free. It is therefore both a practice and a
  • state: the ultimate letting-go that reveals what was never bound.
  • Satya-pratiṣṭhāyāṁ kriyā-phala-āśrayatvam 2.36*
  • When truthfulness is ﬁrmly established, action and result come to depend on the yogi.
  • _Achievement_: Satya here means correspondence between thought, word, and deed
  • rooted in seeing things as they are. When it is perfected, the yogi’s word gains _vāk-siddhi_.
  • Speech is no longer separate from reality, so whatever he says tends to manifest. Vyāsa
  • says: if he tells a virtuous person “Be righteous, ” the person becomes righteous; if he tells a
  • sick person “Be healed, ” health follows. This is not magic, but the power of a mind without
  • self-deception — a mind aligned with _ṛta_, cosmic order.
  • Fold one leg: Bend the left knee and place the left sole against the inner right thigh. Left
  • heel touches the perineum, left knee rests on the ﬂoor. Keep both sit bones grounded.
  • Hand placement: Bend elbows, place palms on the ﬂoor beside your ears. Fingers point
  • toward shoulders. Elbows point up, shoulder-width.
  • Arms up: Inhale, raise arms overhead. Lift chest, look up.
questions.final_answer: Arms up: Inhale, raise arms overhead. Lift chest, look up.

questions.question: Va chitham.
questions.solution_html:
• Asteya-pratiṣṭhāyāṁ sarva-ratna-upasthānam 2.37*
  • When non-stealing is ﬁrmly established, all jewels present themselves.
  • _Achievement_: Asteya is freedom from covetousness, even in thought. When the yogi truly
  • wants nothing that is not his, the sense of lack ends. The sūtra indicates that wealth in all
  • forms — material, intellectual, spiritual — ﬂows toward such a person unsought. Because
  • he has no “hole” of desire, prakṛti ﬁlls him. On a practical level, trustworthiness attracts
  • resources, opportunities, and people’s conﬁdence.
  • Square the torso: Turn your torso slightly so the navel aligns with the center of the right
  • thigh, not twisted to the side.
  • Inhale & lift: Press ﬁrmly into palms and feet. On an inhale, lift the hips, then the torso
  • and head oƯ the ﬂoor. Crown of the head rests lightly on the ﬂoor. Pause this is bridge on
  • head.
  • Bend back: Exhale, push hips forward and begin arching back. Keep thighs and buttocks
  • ﬁrm.
questions.final_answer: ﬁrm.

questions.question: What is ‘Aparigraha’?
questions.solution_html:
• Brahmacarya-pratiṣṭhāyāṁ vīrya-lābhaḥ 2.38 Ceibacy/continence is ﬁrmly established
  • vigor is gained.
  • _Achievement_: Brahmacarya is literally “moving in Brahman. ” It means conserving and
  • sublimating life-energy instead of dissipating it through the senses. When ﬁrmly
  • established, the yogi gains _vīrya_ — not just physical stamina, but intellectual brilliance
  • unshakable will, and spiritual power to transmit knowledge. The nervous system, no longer
  • depleted, can hold higher states of samādhi. Thus brahmacarya becomes the battery for all
  • other limbs.
  • Inhale & lengthen: Raise both arms overhead, stretch the spine upward, lift the chest.
  • Full pose: Exhale. Press more into hands and feet, straighten the arms, and lift the head
  • completely oƯ the ﬂoor. Come into a full arch.
  • Walk down: Place hands on the wall, and slowly walk them down toward the ﬂoor. Keep
  • breathing.
questions.final_answer: breathing.

questions.question: yamaniyama ----- ---- ---- ---- dhyanasamadhayoastavangani.
questions.solution_html:
• Asana- Pranayama – Pratyahra,Dhara na
  • Aparigraha-sthairye janma-kathantā-sambodhaḥ 2.39
  • When non-possessiveness is stabilized, knowledge of the ‘how’ of births arises.
  • Achievement: Aparigraha is freedom from accumulation, seeing the defects in hoarding
  • anxiety of acquiring, protecting, losing, and attachment. When it is stable, the craving that
  • drives rebirth is thinned. Consequently, memory of past lives dawns, because the veil of
  • _tṛṣṇā_ that caused identiﬁcation with one body lifts. The yogi understands the causal
  • chain of his births — “how and why I was born” — which accelerates dispassion and
  • progress to kaivalya.
  • The ﬁve siddhis show that morality in yoga is not imposed social rule, but _natural law_.
  • Each yama removes a speciﬁc color of _kleśa_: violence from dveṣa, lying from rāga-dveṣa
  • stealing from lobha, incontinence from kāma, hoarding from abhiniveśa. As the kleśas thin
  • the powers appear spontaneously, without being sought. Hence Patañjali never calls them
  • “miracles”; they are _pariṇāma_, natural transformations of a puriﬁed citta.
  • Moreover, the yamas protect the yogi and society. A person established in yama becomes a
  • sanctuary others feel safe, truthful, generous near him. Thus the ﬁrst limb itself begins
  • _loka-saṅgraha_, welfare of the world.
  • Conclusion
  • Firmly established yamas are not the end of yoga, but they prove that inner transformation
  • has external consequence. They convert ethics into energy: ahiṁsā into peace, satya into
  • creative word, asteya into abundance, brahmacarya into power, aparigraha into wisdom.
  • These achievements are milestones that the mind is ready for āsana, prāṇāyāma, and the
  • inward limbs. In that sense, the “fruits of yama” are both grace and veriﬁcation — evidence
  • that the yogi is no longer practicing yoga, but has begun to become yoga itself.
  • Exhale & fold: Hinging from the hips, not the waist, extend forward over the right leg.
  • Catch the right foot, ankle, or shin — wherever you reach without rounding the back.
  • Align: Keep feet parallel, knees over ankles. Try to straighten elbows and knees as much
  • as possible. Push the chest toward the wall behind you. Gaze to the ﬂoor or between
  • hands.
  • To ﬂoor: When hands reach the ﬂoor, adjust feet if needed and press into full
  • Chakrāsana.
questions.final_answer: Chakrāsana.

questions.question: What is the achievement of ‘santosa’?
questions.solution_html:
• Head position: In the ﬁnal pose, forehead rests toward the knee/shin. Keep the right foot
  • ﬂexed, toes pointing up.
  • Hold: Breathe normally for 10-30 seconds initially. Don’t hold the breath.
  • Come up: To exit, either walk hands back up the wall, or drop to the ﬂoor and lower as in
  • Method 1.
  • Method 3: With Partner/Props For Support. Wall: Lie with head near a wall. In step 4, place
  • hands on the wall ﬁrst, then press up. Reduces fear and wrist strain. Blocks: Place 2 blocks
  • against a wall at 45°. Rest hands on blocks to reduce wrist extension. Partner: A partner
  • can stand by your hips, hands under your sacrum, and help lift you until your arms gain
  • strength.
  • Key Alignment & Safety Points: Warm-up mandatory*: Do Bhujangāsana, Setu
  • Bandhāsana, Uṣṭrāsana, and shoulder openers ﬁrst.
  • Weight distribution: 60% on legs, 40% on arms. If wrists hurt, shift more weight to legs.
  • Don’t: Force the arms straight if shoulders are tight. Don’t let knees splay out — keep them
  • hip-width.
  • Neck: Keep it neutral. Don’t hang the head or compress the cervical spine.
  • Contraindications: Avoid with wrist, shoulder, or back injury, high BP , heart problems
  • hernia, vertigo, recent surgery, or pregnancy.
  • Counterpose: Always follow with a gentle forward bend like Bālāsana or Paścimottānāsana
  • to release the spine.
  • Practiced correctly, Chakrāsana builds strength, opens the chest and heart area
  • stimulates the nervous system, and improves spinal ﬂexibility.
questions.final_answer: stimulates the nervous system, and improves spinal ﬂexibility.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of shavasana?
questions.solution_html:
• Śavāsana relaxes the entire body and mind, removes fatigue, and integrates the beneﬁts
  • of the yoga practice by bringing the nervous system into deep rest.
  • Hold: Breathe slowly for 30 sec – 2 min. Keep the back as long as possible. With each
  • exhale, soften deeper into the fold.
  • Release: Tuck chin to chest, bend elbows and knees slowly, and lower the spine vertebra
  • by vertebra upper back, middle back, then hips. Rest in Śavāsanaor hug knees to chest to
  • neutralize.
  • Method 2: From Standing – Advanced.Only after mastering the lying version
questions.final_answer: Method 2: From Standing – Advanced.Only after mastering the lying version

questions.question: How long should one hold on Bhujangasana ?
questions.solution_html:
• Hold Bhujangāsana for 15-30 seconds initially, breathing normally; with practice it can
  • be held up to 1 minute.
  • Release: Inhale, lift the torso up. Exhale, release arms. Repeat on the other side.
  • Key Alignment Points
  • Don’t force: If hamstrings are tight, bend the straight knee slightly or use a strap around the
  • foot.
  • Spine ﬁrst: Aim to bring the belly to the thigh before the head to the knee. A rounded spine
  • defeats the beneﬁt.
  • Grounded knee: The bent knee should stay on the ﬂoor. Place a folded blanket under it if
  • needed.
  • Contraindications: Avoid with slipped disc, sciatica, acute knee injury, asthma attack, or
  • diarrhea. Pregnant women should keep the legs wide and not compress the abdomen.
  • Beneﬁts:Jānuśīrṣāsana combines a therapeutic abdominal massage with a deep spinal
  • and hamstring release, calming the mind while toning the digestive organs* . Practiced
  • regularly, it brings ﬂexibility to the body and tranquility to the mind.
questions.final_answer: regularly, it brings ﬂexibility to the body and tranquility to the mind.

questions.question: Recall the number and definition of Niyamangas.
questions.solution_html:
• Niyama is the second limb of Patañjali’s Aṣṭāṅga Yoga_ 2.29. There are ﬁve Niyamas
  • listed in Yoga Sūtra_2.32: Śauca-santoṣa-tapaḥ-svādhyāya-īśvara-praṇidhānāni niyamāḥ.

questions.question: How does Paschimottanasana help improve digestion?
questions.solution_html:
• Paschimottanasana improves digestion by compressing the abdominal organs during
  • the forward fold, which massages the stomach, intestines, liver, and pancreas, stimulating
  • agni or digestive ﬁre and enhancing peristalsis. The pose also activates the
  • parasympathetic nervous system, reducing stress-related digestive issues like bloating and
  • constipation, while the gentle pressure helps relieve trapped gas and improves blood
  • circulation to the digestive tract.
questions.final_answer: circulation to the digestive tract.

questions.question: How does Gomukhasana improve posture?
questions.solution_html:
• Gomukhāsana improves posture by directly opening the chest and stretching the tight
  • muscles . The arm position draws the shoulder blades down and together, counteracting
  • rounded shoulders from desk work, and the lifted spine encourages length through the
  • thoracic region. With the hips and legs grounded, the pose also balances pelvic alignment
  • so the beneﬁts extend from the sit bones to the crown of the head, training the body to
  • maintain an upright, open-chested stance even after leave the mat.
questions.final_answer: maintain an upright, open-chested stance even after leave the mat.

questions.question: How Padmasana is beneficial in improving blood circulation?
questions.solution_html:
• Padmāsana improves blood circulation by redirecting blood ﬂow through the way the
  • legs are folded and locked. With the ankles pressing against the femoral arteries near the
  • groin, circulation to the lower legs is gently restricted, which increases venous return and
  • channels more blood toward the abdominal and pelvic organs — the digestive system
  • reproductive organs, and spine. The upright, stable spine in the pose also reduces
  • muscular eƯort needed for sitting, calming the nervous system and allowing the heart to
  • pump more eƯiciently without the strain of poor posture. Over time, this enhanced ﬂow to
  • the core helps reduce swelling in the legs and promotes better oxygenation of the vital
  • organs.
questions.final_answer: organs.

questions.question: Write an essay on Asamprajnata samadhi?
questions.solution_html:
• In Patañjali’s Yoga Sūtra, samādhi is the culmination of the eight-limbed path of yoga. It
  • is divided into two principal stages: samprajñāta and asamprajñāta. While samprajñāta
  • samādhi is “cognitive” absorption with a support or object, asamprajñāta samādhi is the
  • higher, objectless state often called nirbīja samādhi or “seedless absorption” . It represents
  • the threshold of kaivalya, the ﬁnal liberation of the seer from identiﬁcation with prakṛti.
  • Patañjali deﬁnes it in Yoga Sūtra1.18: Virāma-pratyaya-abhyāsa-pūrvaḥ saṁskāra-śeṣo
  • anyaḥ. “The other samādhi, preceded by the practice of the notion of cessation, has only
  • residual impressions. ”Vyāsa’s commentary clariﬁes: here every vṛtti_of the mind, including
  • the subtle supports used in samprajñāta samādhi, has ceased. Only saṁskāraslatent
  • impressions — remain, but even they are inactive. Because no new mental content arises
  • it isasamprajñāta, “beyond cognition” . It is nirbīja, “seedless, ” because the seeds of future
  • karma and rebirth the kleśas and their saṁskāras are rendered steri.
  • Samprajñāta samādhi still operates within the realm of prakṛti. It has four stages based on
  • the object of meditation: _vitarka_ with gross objects, _vicāra_ with subtle, _ānanda_ with
  • bliss, and _asmitā_ with pure I-sense 1.17. The mind is one-pointed, but still dependent on
  • an _ālambana_, a support.In asamprajñāta, that support itself is dropped. The method is
  • _virāma-pratyaya_ — the “idea of cessation” . The yogi repeatedly turns awareness to the
  • gap between thoughts, to the cessation itself, until the habit of cognition dissolves. What
  • remains is not unconsciousness, but pure awareness without content. Hence it is also
  • called nirvikalpa samādhi in later traditions.
  • Patañjali gives two routes to asamprajñāta in 1.19-1.20
questions.final_answer: Patañjali gives two routes to asamprajñāta in 1.19-1.20

questions.question: Write an essay on the achievements of firmly established Yamangas.
questions.solution_html:
• In Aṣṭāṅga Yoga, _yama_ forms the ethical foundation — the ﬁrst limb without which
  • the later limbs cannot mature. Patañjali lists ﬁve yamas: _ahiṁsā, satya, asteya
  • brahmacarya,_ and _aparigraha_ 2.30. These are called _mahāvrata_, the “great vows, ”
  • when practiced universally without exception 2.31. When a yama becomes _pratiṣṭhā_
  • ﬁrmly established in the yogi’s being, it yields speciﬁc _siddhis_ or fruits that are both
  • psychological transformations and objective changes in the yogi’s environment. Patañjali
  • dedicates sūtras 2.35-2.39 to these achievements.
questions.final_answer: dedicates sūtras 2.35-2.39 to these achievements.
